short_meanings: widespread throughout a place or system
hero.one_line_summary: Pervasive describes something that spreads through or affects many parts of a place, society, system, or situation.
hero.memorable_example: Smartphones have had a pervasive influence on modern communication.

meanings.sense_title: Widespread throughout a place or system
meanings.definition: spreading through or affecting many parts of a place, group, system, or situation
examples: Smartphones have had a pervasive influence on modern communication.
The report describes a pervasive sense of distrust among employees.
Air pollution remains a pervasive problem in many large cities.
Researchers found that social inequality was pervasive throughout the region.
A pervasive smell of smoke remained in the building after the fire.
The study examined the pervasive effects of advertising on consumer behavior.
Corruption had become pervasive across several levels of government.
The internet has become a pervasive part of everyday life.
meanings.typical_pattern: pervasive + influence, problem, effect, presence, attitude, or sense
meanings.register: formal; common in academic, social, political, environmental, and professional writing

nuance.central_nuance: Pervasive does not simply mean common. It suggests that something has spread deeply or widely enough to be present in many different parts of a system or environment.
nuance.usual_implication: The word is often used for problems, influences, attitudes, or effects that are difficult to avoid because they are widely present.
nuance.contrast_explanation: An isolated problem exists only in a limited place or situation. A pervasive problem is widespread and affects many different areas or people.

grammar.how_to_use: Use it before a noun, as in a pervasive influence, or after a linking verb, as in The problem is pervasive.
grammar.what_can_follow: It commonly describes influence, effect, problem, presence, attitude, belief, culture, smell, atmosphere, or feeling.
grammar.preposition_note: When describing where something is widespread, use throughout, across, or in, as in pervasive throughout society.
grammar.position_note: Words such as highly, increasingly, deeply, and extremely can appear before pervasive.

patterns.use: Use this for an influence that affects many areas of life or behavior.
patterns.example: Mass media has a pervasive influence on public attitudes.

patterns.use: Use this for a problem that exists widely throughout a society, organization, or system.
patterns.example: Housing insecurity is a pervasive problem in many rapidly growing cities.

patterns.use: Use this when a feeling is shared widely by many people.
patterns.example: There was a pervasive sense of uncertainty after the announcement.

patterns.pattern: be pervasive throughout + place or system
patterns.use: Use this when emphasizing that something exists in many parts of a larger whole.
patterns.example: The practice was pervasive throughout the industry.

patterns.use: Use this for consequences that spread across many areas.
patterns.example: The researchers studied the pervasive effects of prolonged drought on rural communities.

errors.wrong: The problem is pervasive in only one small department.
errors.correct: The problem is limited to one small department.
errors.explanation: Pervasive suggests that something is widespread, so it is usually inappropriate for something restricted to one small area.

errors.wrong: Technology has pervasively influence on education.
errors.correct: Technology has a pervasive influence on education.
errors.explanation: Use the adjective pervasive before the noun influence.

errors.wrong: Pollution is a pervasive throughout the city.
errors.correct: Pollution is pervasive throughout the city.
errors.explanation: Pervasive is an adjective, so do not use a before it unless it directly modifies a countable noun.
Use the adjective pervasive after was. Pervasively is an adverb.

word_family.definition: to spread through and be present in every or many parts of something
examples: A strong smell of smoke pervaded the building.
A sense of optimism pervaded the organization after the announcement.
Digital technology now pervades many aspects of daily life.
word_family.relationship_to_headword: Pervade is the verb from which pervasive is formed.
word_family.grammar_pattern: pervade + place, system, atmosphere, or aspect of life
word_family.usage_note: It is formal and often used for smells, feelings, attitudes, influences, and ideas.

word_family.definition: the quality of existing or spreading throughout many parts of a place, system, or situation
examples: The study highlights the pervasiveness of digital technology in modern life.
Researchers were surprised by the pervasiveness of the problem across different age groups.
word_family.relationship_to_headword: This noun names the quality of being pervasive.
word_family.grammar_pattern: the pervasiveness of + influence, problem, technology, or practice
word_family.usage_note: It is formal and mainly used in academic or analytical writing.

word_family.definition: in a way that spreads through or affects many parts of something
examples: Digital systems are now pervasively integrated into modern workplaces.
The belief was pervasively present across the organization.
word_family.relationship_to_headword: This adverb describes something that exists or operates in a widespread way.
word_family.grammar_pattern: pervasively + present, distributed, integrated, or used
word_family.usage_note: It is much less common than pervasive.

synonyms.applies_to_sense: Widespread throughout a place or system
synonyms.difference: Widespread means existing in many places or among many people. Pervasive often goes further by suggesting that something has spread deeply through many parts of a system or environment.
synonyms.example: The policy received widespread public support.
synonyms.shared_meaning: Both describe something that exists over a large area or among many people.

synonyms.applies_to_sense: Widespread throughout a place or system
synonyms.difference: Prevalent means common or frequently found in a particular group or place. Pervasive emphasizes how extensively something spreads through or affects the whole environment.
synonyms.example: The disease is particularly prevalent among older adults.
synonyms.shared_meaning: Both can describe something commonly found across a population or area.

synonyms.applies_to_sense: Widespread throughout a place or system
synonyms.difference: Ubiquitous means seeming to be everywhere. Pervasive emphasizes spreading through and influencing many parts of a system or situation.
synonyms.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in many countries.
synonyms.shared_meaning: Both describe something that is present very widely.

synonyms.applies_to_sense: Widespread throughout a place or system
synonyms.difference: Extensive means covering a large amount, area, or range. Pervasive specifically suggests that something penetrates or affects many different parts of a whole.
synonyms.example: The storm caused extensive damage across the region.
synonyms.shared_meaning: Both can describe something that reaches a large area or scope.

antonyms.applies_to_sense: Widespread throughout a place or system
antonyms.opposition: Isolated describes something limited to a small number of cases or locations, while pervasive describes something spread throughout many parts of a system or area.
antonyms.example: Investigators concluded that the failures were isolated incidents rather than evidence of a larger problem.

antonyms.applies_to_sense: Widespread throughout a place or system
antonyms.opposition: Localized means restricted to a particular place or area, while pervasive means widely present across many areas.
antonyms.example: The environmental damage remained localized near the factory.

confusables.key_difference: Prevalent means common or frequently occurring. Pervasive suggests something is not only common but spread deeply or widely through many parts of a system or environment.
confusables.headword_example: A pervasive culture of mistrust affected every department.
confusables.confusable_example: Seasonal allergies are prevalent during the spring.
confusables.why_confused: Both are formal adjectives used to describe things that are common or widespread.

confusables.key_difference: Pervasive describes something widespread throughout a system. Persuasive, which has a similar spelling, means able to convince people.
confusables.headword_example: The report identified a pervasive problem with workplace stress.
confusables.confusable_example: The researcher presented a persuasive argument for changing the policy.
confusables.why_confused: Pervasive and persuasive look and sound somewhat similar but have unrelated meanings.

etymology.origin: Pervasive comes from the Latin verb pervadere, meaning to go through or spread through.
etymology.memory_link: Think of something pervasive as spreading through many parts of a place or system.

word_family_choice.prompt_sentence: A strong smell of smoke seemed to _____ the entire building.
word_family_choice.completed_sentence: A strong smell of smoke seemed to pervade the entire building.
word_family_choice.explanation: Use the verb pervade after to.

word_family_choice.prompt_sentence: The study examined the _____ of digital technology in modern education.
word_family_choice.completed_sentence: The study examined the pervasiveness of digital technology in modern education.
word_family_choice.explanation: Use the noun pervasiveness after the.

word_family_choice.prompt_sentence: The problem had become _____ throughout the organization.
word_family_choice.completed_sentence: The problem had become pervasive throughout the organization.
word_family_choice.explanation: Use the adjective pervasive after become.

correct_or_incorrect.sentence: The organization faced a pervasive culture of distrust.
correct_or_incorrect.explanation: Pervasive correctly describes a culture that exists widely throughout the organization.

correct_or_incorrect.sentence: The problem was pervasive in one isolated office and nowhere else.
correct_or_incorrect.corrected_sentence: The problem was limited to one isolated office and occurred nowhere else.
correct_or_incorrect.explanation: Pervasive implies that something is widespread, not restricted to one small location.

correct_or_incorrect.sentence: Digital technology has had a pervasive influence on modern society.
correct_or_incorrect.explanation: Pervasive influence is a natural collocation for an influence that reaches many areas of life.

correct_or_incorrect.sentence: The report showed that unemployment was very pervasively.
correct_or_incorrect.corrected_sentence: The report showed that unemployment was very pervasive.
correct_or_incorrect.explanation: Use the adjective pervasive after was.

collocation_practice.completed_sentence: The investigation revealed a pervasive culture of secrecy throughout the organization.
collocation_practice.explanation: A pervasive culture is a set of attitudes or practices found widely across a group.

collocation_practice.prompt_sentence: There was a pervasive sense _____ uncertainty among the employees.
collocation_practice.completed_sentence: There was a pervasive sense of uncertainty among the employees.
collocation_practice.explanation: Use a pervasive sense of followed by a feeling or condition.

collocation_practice.prompt_sentence: The practice became pervasive _____ the entire industry.
collocation_practice.completed_sentence: The practice became pervasive throughout the entire industry.
collocation_practice.explanation: Pervasive throughout emphasizes that something exists in many parts of a larger system.

collocation_practice.prompt_sentence: Researchers studied the pervasive _____ of advertising on consumer behavior.
collocation_practice.completed_sentence: Researchers studied the pervasive effects of advertising on consumer behavior.
collocation_practice.explanation: Pervasive effects are consequences that reach many different areas.
